meta.extraction: rule-based lexicon + role rules (pefkg/ontology.py, pefkg/extract.py); no NER/RE library

entity_types.Paper: A publication in the corpus. Carries year, lead author, contribution type and derived scores.
entity_types.Mechanism: A concrete technical move (e.g. low-rank weight update, soft prompt, 4-bit quantization).
entity_types.MechanismFamily: Coarser grouping of mechanisms by *where in the model / training stack* they act.
entity_types.Problem: An obstacle a paper says it addresses (e.g. training memory, inference latency, forgetting).
entity_types.Concept: An idea that other work rests on (e.g. intrinsic dimensionality, scaling laws).
entity_types.Model: A backbone family used as the thing being adapted (BERT, T5, GPT-3, LLaMA ...).
entity_types.Benchmark: A dataset or suite on which methods are evaluated.
entity_types.Author: Lead author of a paper (the bootstrap corpus stores lead authors only).

relation_types.PROPOSES: Paper -> Mechanism. The mechanism is part of the paper's own contribution (named in the title or in the first 'we propose/introduce' sentence).
relation_types.USES: Paper -> Mechanism. Mechanism is used as a component / substrate but is not the contribution.
relation_types.COVERS: Survey -> Mechanism. A survey describes the mechanism; it neither proposes nor uses it.
relation_types.COMPARES_WITH: Paper -> Mechanism. Mechanism appears only in a contrastive sentence (unlike / compared with / outperforms / without ...), i.e. as a baseline or foil.
relation_types.ADDRESSES: Paper -> Problem. The problem is named as motivation or as a measured outcome.
relation_types.ESTABLISHES: Paper -> Concept. The paper introduces or demonstrates the concept.
relation_types.RELIES_ON: Paper -> Concept. The paper assumes or motivates itself with the concept.
relation_types.INTRODUCES_MODEL: Paper -> Model. Foundation-model paper that introduces the model family.
relation_types.USES_MODEL: Paper -> Model. Model family is adapted or evaluated in the paper.
relation_types.EVALUATED_ON: Paper -> Benchmark. Paper reports results on the benchmark.
relation_types.EXTENDS: A refines a mechanism that B also proposes (shared PROPOSES). Strong prerequisite.
relation_types.BUILDS_ON: A uses a mechanism that B proposes as a component/substrate. Strong prerequisite.
relation_types.COMPARES_WITH_PAPER: A positions itself against the mechanism B proposes (baseline / alternative). Not a prerequisite; a 'must compare' pointer.
relation_types.MOTIVATED_BY: A rests on a concept B establishes, or on B's empirical analysis of a mechanism A uses. Prerequisite.
relation_types.USES_BACKBONE: A adapts / evaluates on a model family B introduces. Prerequisite for beginners only.
relation_types.USES_BENCHMARK: A evaluates on a benchmark B introduces. Reference only.
relation_types.SURVEYS: A is a survey and B is one of the works it covers. Never a prerequisite.
relation_types.BACKGROUND: Citation with no structural link in the schema. Weakest edge.
relation_types.UNDERPINS: Concept -> Mechanism. Hand-authored background knowledge (see CONCEPT_UNDERPINS).

mechanism_families.ADDITIVE: Inject new trainable parameters; the backbone stays frozen.
mechanism_families.SELECTIVE: Train only a chosen subset of the existing parameters.
mechanism_families.REPARAMETERIZATION: Express the weight update in a cheaper form (low-rank, shared, decomposed ...).
mechanism_families.COMPRESSION: Shrink the numeric representation of the model.
mechanism_families.COMPOSITION: Combine, route or transfer between separately trained modules.
mechanism_families.TRAINING_RECIPE_AND_SYSTEMS: Change how training / serving is executed (memory, optimizer, schedule, kernels) rather than what is learned.
mechanism_families.SUPERVISION: Change the data or objective used to adapt a model.
mechanism_families.HYBRID: Unify or jointly use several families.

transformer.title: Attention Is All You Need
transformer.claim_sentence: Proposes the Transformer, a network architecture built entirely on self-attention that dispenses with recurrence and convolutions.
transformer.abstract: Proposes the Transformer, a network architecture built entirely on self-attention that dispenses with recurrence and convolutions. It trains faster than recurrent models and sets new quality records on machine translation.

ulmfit.title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
ulmfit.claim_sentence: Proposes ULMFiT, a transfer learning method for NLP that fine-tunes a pretrained language model with discriminative fine-tuning, slanted triangular learning rates and gradual unfreezing.
ulmfit.abstract: Proposes ULMFiT, a transfer learning method for NLP that fine-tunes a pretrained language model with discriminative fine-tuning, slanted triangular learning rates and gradual unfreezing. It cuts error on text classification with far less labeled data and limits catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning.

bert.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
bert.claim_sentence: Introduces BERT, a language representation model pre-trained with a masked language modeling objective that conditions on both left and right context.
bert.abstract: Introduces BERT, a language representation model pre-trained with a masked language modeling objective that conditions on both left and right context. A pre-trained BERT fine-tuned with one extra output layer sets new results on GLUE and other language understanding tasks.

glue.title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding
glue.claim_sentence: Introduces GLUE, a collection of nine sentence-level language understanding tasks with a diagnostic dataset for analyzing models across tasks.
glue.abstract: Introduces GLUE, a collection of nine sentence-level language understanding tasks with a diagnostic dataset for analyzing models across tasks. Baselines trained with multi-task learning and transfer from pretrained representations show that existing methods still struggle to share knowledge across tasks.

gpt2.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
gpt2.claim_sentence: Presents GPT-2, a 1.5 billion parameter Transformer language model trained on a large web text corpus.
gpt2.abstract: Presents GPT-2, a 1.5 billion parameter Transformer language model trained on a large web text corpus. It performs many tasks in a zero-shot setting without task-specific training, suggesting that scaling language models is a path toward general multitask systems.

t5.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
t5.claim_sentence: Introduces a text-to-text framework that casts every language task as generating text, and systematically compares pre-training objectives, architectures and data.
t5.abstract: Introduces a text-to-text framework that casts every language task as generating text, and systematically compares pre-training objectives, architectures and data. The resulting T5 models, scaled to 11 billion parameters and pre-trained on a large cleaned web corpus, reach strong results on GLUE and SuperGLUE.

superglue.title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems
superglue.claim_sentence: Introduces SuperGLUE, a harder successor to GLUE with more difficult language understanding tasks, a public leaderboard and human performance baselines, created after models surpassed human-level scores on GLUE.
superglue.abstract: Introduces SuperGLUE, a harder successor to GLUE with more difficult language understanding tasks, a public leaderboard and human performance baselines, created after models surpassed human-level scores on GLUE.

scaling_laws.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
scaling_laws.claim_sentence: Shows that language model loss follows power-law relationships with model size, dataset size and training compute, and that larger models are more sample-efficient.
scaling_laws.abstract: Shows that language model loss follows power-law relationships with model size, dataset size and training compute, and that larger models are more sample-efficient. Derives how to split a fixed compute allowance across these factors.

gpt3.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
gpt3.claim_sentence: Trains GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, and evaluates it in the few-shot setting where tasks are specified through text demonstrations with no gradient updates.
gpt3.abstract: Trains GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, and evaluates it in the few-shot setting where tasks are specified through text demonstrations with no gradient updates. It performs strongly on many tasks but still falls short on some, showing the promise of in-context learning.

mmlu.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
mmlu.claim_sentence: Introduces MMLU, a benchmark of multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects spanning STEM, humanities and social sciences, used to test knowledge acquired during pretraining in zero-shot and few-shot settings.
mmlu.abstract: Introduces MMLU, a benchmark of multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects spanning STEM, humanities and social sciences, used to test knowledge acquired during pretraining in zero-shot and few-shot settings. The largest models of the time scored only modestly above chance.

flan.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
flan.claim_sentence: Introduces FLAN, a 137B model produced by instruction tuning on a collection of datasets phrased as natural language instructions.
flan.abstract: Introduces FLAN, a 137B model produced by instruction tuning on a collection of datasets phrased as natural language instructions. It substantially improves zero-shot performance on unseen task types, with gains that depend on the number of tuning tasks and on model scale.

instructgpt.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
instructgpt.claim_sentence: Introduces InstructGPT, models obtained by fine-tuning GPT-3 with supervised examples and reinforcement learning from human feedback so that outputs follow user intent.
instructgpt.abstract: Introduces InstructGPT, models obtained by fine-tuning GPT-3 with supervised examples and reinforcement learning from human feedback so that outputs follow user intent. Human evaluators prefer outputs from a 1.3B InstructGPT model over the 175B GPT-3, with improvements in truthfulness and fewer toxic outputs.

flan_scaling.title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
flan_scaling.claim_sentence: Introduces Flan-T5 and Flan-PaLM by scaling instruction finetuning along three axes: the number of tasks, the model size, and finetuning on chain-of-thought data.
flan_scaling.abstract: Introduces Flan-T5 and Flan-PaLM by scaling instruction finetuning along three axes: the number of tasks, the model size, and finetuning on chain-of-thought data. Flan-T5 and Flan-PaLM improve over their base models on held-out benchmarks such as MMLU and BIG-Bench Hard.

chinchilla.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
chinchilla.claim_sentence: Finds that model size and training tokens should be scaled in equal proportion for a given compute allowance, and shows that a 70B model trained on more data outperforms much larger models trained on fewer tokens.
chinchilla.abstract: Finds that model size and training tokens should be scaled in equal proportion for a given compute allowance, and shows that a 70B model trained on more data outperforms much larger models trained on fewer tokens.

llama.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
llama.claim_sentence: Introduces LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models from 7B to 65B parameters trained on publicly available data only.
llama.abstract: Introduces LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models from 7B to 65B parameters trained on publicly available data only. The 13B model outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks, and the 65B model is competitive with the best models of its time.

llama2.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
llama2.claim_sentence: Releases Llama 2, a family of pretrained and dialogue-tuned language models from 7B to 70B parameters, with a detailed description of the safety-oriented tuning approach.
llama2.abstract: Releases Llama 2, a family of pretrained and dialogue-tuned language models from 7B to 70B parameters, with a detailed description of the safety-oriented tuning approach. The chat models outperform most open models on helpfulness and safety evaluations.

self_instruct.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
self_instruct.claim_sentence: Proposes a framework in which a pretrained model bootstraps its own instruction data by generating instructions, inputs and outputs, filtering low-quality samples and fine-tuning on the result.
self_instruct.abstract: Proposes a framework in which a pretrained model bootstraps its own instruction data by generating instructions, inputs and outputs, filtering low-quality samples and fine-tuning on the result. Applied to GPT-3, it yields a large improvement on unseen tasks without relying on costly human-written instructions.

lima.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
lima.claim_sentence: Introduces LIMA, a 65B LLaMA model fine-tuned on only 1,000 carefully curated prompts and responses, which obtains strong chat behavior with no further alignment stage.
lima.abstract: Introduces LIMA, a 65B LLaMA model fine-tuned on only 1,000 carefully curated prompts and responses, which obtains strong chat behavior with no further alignment stage. Suggests that almost all knowledge is learned during pretraining and only limited instruction data is needed to teach output style.

superficial_alignment.match: almost all knowledge is learned during pretraining

adapters.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
adapters.claim_sentence: Proposes adapter modules, small bottleneck layers inserted between the layers of a pretrained BERT model, so that only the adapters are trained while the original weights stay frozen.
adapters.abstract: Proposes adapter modules, small bottleneck layers inserted between the layers of a pretrained BERT model, so that only the adapters are trained while the original weights stay frozen. Tasks can be added sequentially, each costing a tiny fraction of the parameters, and the approach nearly matches full fine-tuning on 26 text classification tasks including GLUE.

adapterfusion.title: AdapterFusion: Non-Destructive Task Composition for Transfer Learning
adapterfusion.claim_sentence: Proposes a two-stage method that first learns adapters for individual tasks and then trains a fusion layer that combines the stored adapters with attention, sharing knowledge across tasks without forgetting earlier ones.
adapterfusion.abstract: Proposes a two-stage method that first learns adapters for individual tasks and then trains a fusion layer that combines the stored adapters with attention, sharing knowledge across tasks without forgetting earlier ones. It improves over full fine-tuning and single-task adapters on several language understanding benchmarks.

madx.title: MAD-X: An Adapter-Based Framework for Multi-Task Cross-Lingual Transfer
madx.claim_sentence: Proposes a modular framework that learns language-specific and task-specific adapters plus invertible adapters, which can be stacked to transfer to languages unseen during pretraining.
madx.abstract: Proposes a modular framework that learns language-specific and task-specific adapters plus invertible adapters, which can be stacked to transfer to languages unseen during pretraining. It gains parameter efficiency and outperforms standard transfer on cross-lingual named entity recognition and question answering.

intrinsic_dim.title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
intrinsic_dim.claim_sentence: Shows that pretrained language models can be fine-tuned effectively inside a random low-dimensional subspace using a very small number of parameters, and that more pretraining lowers the intrinsic dimension needed for a task.
intrinsic_dim.abstract: Shows that pretrained language models can be fine-tuned effectively inside a random low-dimensional subspace using a very small number of parameters, and that more pretraining lowers the intrinsic dimension needed for a task. Offers an explanation for why fine-tuning with so few parameters generalizes.

diff_pruning.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning with Diff Pruning
diff_pruning.claim_sentence: Proposes diff pruning, which learns a task-specific sparse difference vector added to fixed pretrained weights, kept sparse with a differentiable L0 penalty.
diff_pruning.abstract: Proposes diff pruning, which learns a task-specific sparse difference vector added to fixed pretrained weights, kept sparse with a differentiable L0 penalty. It modifies only about 0.5% of the parameters per task while matching full fine-tuning on the GLUE benchmark.

prefix_tuning.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
prefix_tuning.claim_sentence: Proposes prefix-tuning, which keeps the language model frozen and optimizes a small continuous task-specific vector, the prefix, that later tokens attend to like virtual tokens.
prefix_tuning.abstract: Proposes prefix-tuning, which keeps the language model frozen and optimizes a small continuous task-specific vector, the prefix, that later tokens attend to like virtual tokens. Tuning 0.1% of the parameters matches full fine-tuning on E2E table-to-text generation with GPT-2 and BART summarization, and does better in low-data settings.

prompt_tuning.title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
prompt_tuning.claim_sentence: Proposes prompt tuning, which learns soft prompts as extra input embeddings for a frozen T5 model.
prompt_tuning.abstract: Proposes prompt tuning, which learns soft prompts as extra input embeddings for a frozen T5 model. As models grow past billions of parameters it closes the gap to full fine-tuning, outperforming GPT-3 few-shot prompting on SuperGLUE and letting one frozen model serve many tasks.

ptuning.title: GPT Understands, Too
ptuning.claim_sentence: Proposes P-tuning, which trains continuous prompt embeddings produced by a small prompt encoder and inserts them among discrete prompts, since discrete prompts are brittle and unstable.
ptuning.abstract: Proposes P-tuning, which trains continuous prompt embeddings produced by a small prompt encoder and inserts them among discrete prompts, since discrete prompts are brittle and unstable. It improves GPT-style models on knowledge probing and SuperGLUE in fully supervised and few-shot settings, narrowing the gap with similarly sized BERT models.

ptuning_v2.title: P-Tuning v2: Prompt Tuning Can Be Comparable to Fine-tuning Universally Across Scales and Tasks
ptuning_v2.claim_sentence: Proposes P-Tuning v2, which applies deep prompt tuning, continuous prompts at every layer instead of only the input, and matches full fine-tuning from 300M to 10B parameters and on hard sequence-labeling tasks, where earlier prompt tuning lagged behind full fine-tuning.
ptuning_v2.abstract: Proposes P-Tuning v2, which applies deep prompt tuning, continuous prompts at every layer instead of only the input, and matches full fine-tuning from 300M to 10B parameters and on hard sequence-labeling tasks, where earlier prompt tuning lagged behind full fine-tuning.

bitfit.title: BitFit: Simple Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning for Transformer-based Masked Language-models
bitfit.claim_sentence: Proposes BitFit, which updates only the bias terms of a pretrained BERT model, roughly 0.1% of its parameters.
bitfit.abstract: Proposes BitFit, which updates only the bias terms of a pretrained BERT model, roughly 0.1% of its parameters. It matches or comes close to full fine-tuning on GLUE for small and medium data and is competitive with other sparse approaches, suggesting that fine-tuning mainly exposes existing knowledge.

compacter.title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
compacter.claim_sentence: Proposes Compacter, which builds adapter layers from Kronecker products of shared slow weights and low-rank fast weights using hypercomplex multiplication.
compacter.abstract: Proposes Compacter, which builds adapter layers from Kronecker products of shared slow weights and low-rank fast weights using hypercomplex multiplication. It trains only about 0.05% of the parameters of a T5 model while outperforming standard adapters on GLUE and SuperGLUE.

lora.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
lora.claim_sentence: Proposes LoRA, which freezes the pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer.
lora.abstract: Proposes LoRA, which freezes the pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer. The design rests on the observation that weight updates during adaptation have a low intrinsic rank. Compared to fine-tuning GPT-3 175B with Adam it cuts trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory by three times, unlike adapter layers it adds no inference latency, and it performs on par with or better than full fine-tuning on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2 and GPT-3.

unified_view.title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
unified_view.claim_sentence: Proposes a unified framework that casts adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA as modifications to specific hidden states of a frozen model, revealing design dimensions such as the functional form, the insertion position and the composition.
unified_view.abstract: Proposes a unified framework that casts adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA as modifications to specific hidden states of a frozen model, revealing design dimensions such as the functional form, the insertion position and the composition. It uses the framework to derive new variants that match full fine-tuning with 0.5% of the parameters while outperforming existing methods on translation, summarization and understanding tasks.

unipelt.title: UniPELT: A Unified Framework for Parameter-Efficient Language Model Tuning
unipelt.claim_sentence: Proposes a unified framework that incorporates adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA as submodules, activated through a gating mechanism that learns which to use for a given task and setup.
unipelt.abstract: Proposes a unified framework that incorporates adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA as submodules, activated through a gating mechanism that learns which to use for a given task and setup. It outperforms its best individual submodule and full fine-tuning on GLUE, particularly with little training data.

spot.title: SPoT: Better Frozen Model Adaptation through Soft Prompt Transfer
spot.claim_sentence: Proposes soft prompt transfer, which first learns a prompt on source tasks and uses it to initialize the prompt for a target task on a frozen T5 model.
spot.abstract: Proposes soft prompt transfer, which first learns a prompt on source tasks and uses it to initialize the prompt for a target task on a frozen T5 model. It substantially improves prompt tuning on SuperGLUE, matches or beats full fine-tuning across model sizes, and allows predicting which source tasks transfer well.

t_few.title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
t_few.claim_sentence: Proposes T-Few, a recipe built on (IA)3, which rescales inner activations with learned vectors and adds only a tiny number of new parameters, together with new loss terms and no task-specific tuning.
t_few.abstract: Proposes T-Few, a recipe built on (IA)3, which rescales inner activations with learned vectors and adds only a tiny number of new parameters, together with new loss terms and no task-specific tuning. T-Few beats in-context learning with GPT-3 and reaches super-human performance on a few-shot benchmark at far lower inference cost.

delta_tuning.title: Delta Tuning: A Comprehensive Study of Parameter Efficient Methods for Pre-trained Language Models
delta_tuning.claim_sentence: Surveys parameter-efficient methods under the name delta tuning and groups them into addition-based, specification-based and reparameterization-based families, covering adapters, prompt tuning, prefix-tuning, BitFit and LoRA.
delta_tuning.abstract: Surveys parameter-efficient methods under the name delta tuning and groups them into addition-based, specification-based and reparameterization-based families, covering adapters, prompt tuning, prefix-tuning, BitFit and LoRA. It offers theoretical views through optimization and optimal control and evaluates over 100 NLP tasks.

adamix.title: AdaMix: Mixture-of-Adaptations for Parameter-efficient Model Tuning
adamix.claim_sentence: Proposes mixture-of-adaptations, in which several adaptation modules are placed in each layer and randomly routed during training, then merged by weight averaging for inference so no extra cost is paid.
adamix.abstract: Proposes mixture-of-adaptations, in which several adaptation modules are placed in each layer and randomly routed during training, then merged by weight averaging for inference so no extra cost is paid. The modules can be adapters or LoRA. It outperforms full fine-tuning on GLUE while tuning 0.1-0.2% of parameters.

dylora.title: DyLoRA: Parameter Efficient Tuning of Pre-trained Models using Dynamic Search-Free Low-Rank Adaptation
dylora.claim_sentence: Proposes training LoRA blocks for a range of ranks instead of a single fixed rank, by sorting the representation learned at different ranks during training.
dylora.abstract: Proposes training LoRA blocks for a range of ranks instead of a single fixed rank, by sorting the representation learned at different ranks during training. It removes the need to search for the best rank and runs 4 to 7 times faster than LoRA while keeping competitive quality.

adalora.title: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
adalora.claim_sentence: Proposes AdaLoRA, which parameterizes incremental updates in singular value decomposition form and prunes the singular values of unimportant updates, so the rank budget is allocated adaptively across weight matrices according to an importance score.
adalora.abstract: Proposes AdaLoRA, which parameterizes incremental updates in singular value decomposition form and prunes the singular values of unimportant updates, so the rank budget is allocated adaptively across weight matrices according to an importance score. It gives gains over LoRA and other baselines under low parameter budgets on GLUE, question answering and summarization.

llama_adapter.title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention
llama_adapter.claim_sentence: Proposes a method that prepends a set of learnable adaptation prompts to the upper Transformer layers of a frozen LLaMA 7B and uses zero-init attention to inject instruction signals stably.
llama_adapter.abstract: Proposes a method that prepends a set of learnable adaptation prompts to the upper Transformer layers of a frozen LLaMA 7B and uses zero-init attention to inject instruction signals stably. It turns LLaMA into an instruction-following model with 1.2M trainable parameters in under one hour.

scaling_down.title: Scaling Down to Scale Up: A Guide to Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
scaling_down.claim_sentence: Surveys more than forty parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods and organizes them into additive, selective, reparameterization-based and hybrid families, with a comparison of their storage, memory and computation costs.
scaling_down.abstract: Surveys more than forty parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods and organizes them into additive, selective, reparameterization-based and hybrid families, with a comparison of their storage, memory and computation costs. It reports experiments on models up to 11B parameters and discusses open challenges.

peft_survey.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Models: A Comprehensive Survey
peft_survey.claim_sentence: Surveys PEFT algorithms for large models, covering additive, selective, reparameterized and hybrid methods, plus systems and applications in scenarios such as multi-task serving and distributed tuning.
peft_survey.abstract: Surveys PEFT algorithms for large models, covering additive, selective, reparameterized and hybrid methods, plus systems and applications in scenarios such as multi-task serving and distributed tuning. It discusses the computation and memory costs of adapting very large models.

vera.title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation
vera.claim_sentence: Proposes VeRA, which freezes a single pair of random low-rank matrices shared across all layers and trains only small scaling vectors per layer.
vera.abstract: Proposes VeRA, which freezes a single pair of random low-rank matrices shared across all layers and trains only small scaling vectors per layer. It cuts trainable parameters by 10 times compared to LoRA. Performance is kept on GLUE, E2E and instruction tuning of LLaMA models.

lora_fa.title: LoRA-FA: Memory-efficient Low-rank Adaptation for Large Language Models Fine-tuning
lora_fa.claim_sentence: Proposes LoRA-FA, which freezes the down-projection matrix of each LoRA layer and updates only the up-projection, so the activations needed for backpropagation no longer need to be stored in full.
lora_fa.abstract: Proposes LoRA-FA, which freezes the down-projection matrix of each LoRA layer and updates only the up-projection, so the activations needed for backpropagation no longer need to be stored in full. It reduces activation memory by up to 1.4 times with no change in accuracy and without expensive recomputation or quantization.

longlora.title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
longlora.claim_sentence: Proposes shifted sparse attention, which approximates full attention during fine-tuning with sparse local attention over shifted groups, together with an improved LoRA that also trains embeddings and normalization layers.
longlora.abstract: Proposes shifted sparse attention, which approximates full attention during fine-tuning with sparse local attention over shifted groups, together with an improved LoRA that also trains embeddings and normalization layers. Full fine-tuning at long context lengths is prohibitively expensive, and this extends LLaMA 2 7B to 100k tokens and the 70B model to 32k on a single machine.

lorahub.title: LoraHub: Efficient Cross-Task Generalization via Dynamic LoRA Composition
lorahub.claim_sentence: Proposes LoraHub, a framework that composes LoRA modules trained on different upstream tasks using a gradient-free search over a few examples of an unseen task, with no extra parameters or gradient steps.
lorahub.abstract: Proposes LoraHub, a framework that composes LoRA modules trained on different upstream tasks using a gradient-free search over a few examples of an unseen task, with no extra parameters or gradient steps. On Big-Bench Hard it approaches few-shot in-context learning at lower inference cost.

loramoe.title: LoRAMoE: Alleviating World Knowledge Forgetting in Large Language Models via MoE-Style Plugin
loramoe.claim_sentence: Proposes LoRAMoE, which integrates several LoRA experts with a router network and a localized balancing constraint so that some experts preserve world knowledge while others handle downstream tasks.
loramoe.abstract: Proposes LoRAMoE, which integrates several LoRA experts with a router network and a localized balancing constraint so that some experts preserve world knowledge while others handle downstream tasks. It reduces forgetting of world knowledge when scaling up instruction data in supervised fine-tuning of LLaMA-2 models.

s_lora.title: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters
s_lora.claim_sentence: Presents a system for serving many LoRA adapters that keeps all of them in main memory, fetches those needed for active queries into GPU memory, and uses unified paging and custom kernels for heterogeneous batching.
s_lora.abstract: Presents a system for serving many LoRA adapters that keeps all of them in main memory, fetches those needed for active queries into GPU memory, and uses unified paging and custom kernels for heterogeneous batching. It improves throughput by up to 4 times over naive serving of LoRA weights and increases the number of concurrently served LoRA models by orders of magnitude.

relora.title: ReLoRA: High-Rank Training Through Low-Rank Updates
relora.claim_sentence: Proposes ReLoRA, which trains a high-rank network through repeated low-rank updates, merging them into the weights and restarting the optimizer and learning-rate schedule.
relora.abstract: Proposes ReLoRA, which trains a high-rank network through repeated low-rank updates, merging them into the weights and restarting the optimizer and learning-rate schedule. Pre-training large networks from scratch is expensive, and applied to Transformers up to 1.3B parameters it matches regular training while saving memory.

galore.title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
galore.claim_sentence: Proposes GaLore, a training strategy that projects gradients onto a low-rank subspace so that optimizer states take far less memory while all weights are still learned.
galore.abstract: Proposes GaLore, a training strategy that projects gradients onto a low-rank subspace so that optimizer states take far less memory while all weights are still learned. Gradients become low-rank during training, which makes this possible. It cuts optimizer-state memory by up to 65%, allows memory-efficient pre-training from scratch of a 7B model on a single consumer 24GB GPU, and works with 8-bit optimizers. Unlike LoRA, it does not restrict the weights to a low-rank parameterization.

dora.title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
dora.claim_sentence: Proposes DoRA, which decomposes pretrained weights into magnitude and direction and fine-tunes both, applying LoRA only to the directional component.
dora.abstract: Proposes DoRA, which decomposes pretrained weights into magnitude and direction and fine-tunes both, applying LoRA only to the directional component. It narrows the gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning and consistently outperforms LoRA on commonsense reasoning and LLaMA models without adding inference overhead.

lora_plus.title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
lora_plus.claim_sentence: Shows that using the same learning rate for the two LoRA matrices is suboptimal for wide models and proposes setting different learning rates for them, which improves feature learning.
lora_plus.abstract: Shows that using the same learning rate for the two LoRA matrices is suboptimal for wide models and proposes setting different learning rates for them, which improves feature learning. It gains up to 2% accuracy and about 2x speedup over standard LoRA at the same computational cost.

pissa.title: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation of Large Language Models
pissa.claim_sentence: Proposes PiSSA, which initializes the low-rank matrices with the principal singular values and vectors of the pretrained weight matrix and freezes the residual components, so training converges faster and fits better than LoRA.
pissa.abstract: Proposes PiSSA, which initializes the low-rank matrices with the principal singular values and vectors of the pretrained weight matrix and freezes the residual components, so training converges faster and fits better than LoRA. It supports quantized backbones with lower quantization error than QLoRA.

lora_less_forgets.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
lora_less_forgets.claim_sentence: Studies how LoRA compares with full fine-tuning on code and mathematics for continued pretraining and instruction fine-tuning of Llama-2 models.
lora_less_forgets.abstract: Studies how LoRA compares with full fine-tuning on code and mathematics for continued pretraining and instruction fine-tuning of Llama-2 models. LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning but also forgets less of the source domain and keeps more diverse generations, and full fine-tuning learns perturbations with a rank 10 to 100 times greater than typical LoRA configurations.

ewc.title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting in Neural Networks
ewc.claim_sentence: Proposes elastic weight consolidation, which slows learning on weights that were important for earlier tasks through a quadratic penalty, allowing a network to learn tasks sequentially without forgetting old ones.
ewc.abstract: Proposes elastic weight consolidation, which slows learning on weights that were important for earlier tasks through a quadratic penalty, allowing a network to learn tasks sequentially without forgetting old ones. It is shown on supervised MNIST tasks and sequential Atari 2600 games.

grad_checkpoint.title: Training Deep Nets with Sublinear Memory Cost
grad_checkpoint.claim_sentence: Proposes a scheme that drops intermediate activations during the forward pass and recomputes them during backpropagation, reducing memory for an n-layer network to O(sqrt(n)) at the price of one extra forward pass.
grad_checkpoint.abstract: Proposes a scheme that drops intermediate activations during the forward pass and recomputes them during backpropagation, reducing memory for an n-layer network to O(sqrt(n)) at the price of one extra forward pass.

mixed_precision.title: Mixed Precision Training
mixed_precision.claim_sentence: Presents a methodology for training deep networks with half-precision floating point numbers by keeping a single-precision master copy of weights and applying loss scaling to preserve small gradient values.
mixed_precision.abstract: Presents a methodology for training deep networks with half-precision floating point numbers by keeping a single-precision master copy of weights and applying loss scaling to preserve small gradient values. It halves memory use with no loss of accuracy across convolutional, recurrent and generative models.

eightbit_optim.title: 8-bit Optimizers via Block-wise Quantization
eightbit_optim.claim_sentence: Introduces 8-bit optimizers that quantize optimizer states block by block with a dynamic quantization scheme and a stable embedding layer, maintaining 32-bit performance on language modeling, translation and pretraining while cutting optimizer memory by 75%.
eightbit_optim.abstract: Introduces 8-bit optimizers that quantize optimizer states block by block with a dynamic quantization scheme and a stable embedding layer, maintaining 32-bit performance on language modeling, translation and pretraining while cutting optimizer memory by 75%.

llm_int8.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
llm_int8.claim_sentence: Introduces a two-part 8-bit quantization procedure with vector-wise quantization and a mixed-precision decomposition that isolates emergent outlier feature dimensions in 16-bit.
llm_int8.abstract: Introduces a two-part 8-bit quantization procedure with vector-wise quantization and a mixed-precision decomposition that isolates emergent outlier feature dimensions in 16-bit. It enables inference of models up to 175B parameters, such as OPT, with no loss of performance and halves the memory required.

kbit_scaling.title: The Case for 4-bit Precision: k-bit Inference Scaling Laws
kbit_scaling.claim_sentence: Studies the trade-off between model size and bit precision across thousands of inference experiments with OPT, BLOOM, GPT-2 and Pythia, and finds that 4-bit precision is almost universally optimal for total model bits and accuracy.
kbit_scaling.abstract: Studies the trade-off between model size and bit precision across thousands of inference experiments with OPT, BLOOM, GPT-2 and Pythia, and finds that 4-bit precision is almost universally optimal for total model bits and accuracy. It examines data types and block sizes that improve scaling.

gptq.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
gptq.claim_sentence: Proposes GPTQ, a one-shot weight quantization method based on approximate second-order information that compresses GPT models with hundreds of billions of parameters to 3 or 4 bits per weight with negligible accuracy loss in a few GPU hours.
gptq.abstract: Proposes GPTQ, a one-shot weight quantization method based on approximate second-order information that compresses GPT models with hundreds of billions of parameters to 3 or 4 bits per weight with negligible accuracy loss in a few GPU hours. It enables running a 175B-parameter model on a single GPU.

awq.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
awq.claim_sentence: Proposes activation-aware weight quantization, which protects the small fraction of salient weights identified from activation statistics by scaling channels before quantizing, without backpropagation or reconstruction.
awq.abstract: Proposes activation-aware weight quantization, which protects the small fraction of salient weights identified from activation statistics by scaling channels before quantizing, without backpropagation or reconstruction. It keeps small accuracy loss across language and multimodal models and ships with an inference framework that reduces inference latency on edge devices.

qlora.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
qlora.claim_sentence: Introduces QLoRA, which combines a 4-bit NormalFloat data type, double quantization of the quantization constants and paged optimizers to fine-tune large models on a single GPU.
qlora.abstract: Introduces QLoRA, which combines a 4-bit NormalFloat data type, double quantization of the quantization constants and paged optimizers to fine-tune large models on a single GPU. Gradients flow through the frozen quantized weights into LoRA adapters, so a 65B LLaMA model can be fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU while preserving 16-bit fine-tuning quality, and the resulting Guanaco models approach ChatGPT on the Vicuna benchmark.

qa_lora.title: QA-LoRA: Quantization-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
qa_lora.claim_sentence: Proposes quantization-aware low-rank adaptation, using group-wise operators so the quantized weights and the low-rank update share a form that can be merged after fine-tuning without falling back to 16-bit precision.
qa_lora.abstract: Proposes quantization-aware low-rank adaptation, using group-wise operators so the quantized weights and the low-rank update share a form that can be merged after fine-tuning without falling back to 16-bit precision. It keeps the model low-bit, lowers inference latency compared with QLoRA, and reaches comparable or better accuracy on LLaMA and LLaMA2 without the accuracy loss of post-training quantization.

loftq.title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
loftq.claim_sentence: Proposes LoftQ, which quantizes a pretrained model while simultaneously finding a good low-rank initialization of the LoRA matrices that compensates for the quantization error.
loftq.abstract: Proposes LoftQ, which quantizes a pretrained model while simultaneously finding a good low-rank initialization of the LoRA matrices that compensates for the quantization error. It improves downstream results over QLoRA, especially in low-bit regimes such as 2-bit where the zero initialization of QLoRA fails.

lora_init.match: initialization of the lora matrices that compensates for the quantization error

task_arithmetic.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
task_arithmetic.claim_sentence: Proposes task vectors, obtained by subtracting pretrained weights from fine-tuned weights, and shows that adding, negating or combining them steers model behavior, for example removing a skill or building multi-task models, without further training.
task_arithmetic.abstract: Proposes task vectors, obtained by subtracting pretrained weights from fine-tuned weights, and shows that adding, negating or combining them steers model behavior, for example removing a skill or building multi-task models, without further training. It works across vision and language models such as GPT-2 and T5.

adapter_modules.label: Adapter modules
adapter_modules.description: Small bottleneck modules inserted between frozen Transformer layers.

soft_prompt.label: Soft / prefix prompts
soft_prompt.description: Learned continuous vectors prepended to the input or to every layer.

activation_rescaling.label: Learned activation rescaling
activation_rescaling.description: Learned vectors that elementwise rescale internal activations ((IA)^3).

zero_init_gating.label: Zero-initialised gated injection
zero_init_gating.description: Inject new signal through a gate initialised at zero so the pretrained behaviour is preserved at step 0.

sparse_diff.label: Sparse difference vector
sparse_diff.description: Learn a sparse task-specific delta over frozen weights.

gradual_unfreezing.label: Gradual unfreezing / discriminative LR
gradual_unfreezing.description: Unfreeze layers progressively with layer-wise learning rates.

low_rank_update.label: Low-rank weight update (LoRA)
low_rank_update.description: Represent the weight update as a product of two thin matrices.

adaptive_rank.label: Adaptive rank / budget allocation
adaptive_rank.description: Choose rank or parameter budget per layer/matrix instead of a uniform fixed rank.

weight_decomposition.label: Magnitude / direction decomposition
weight_decomposition.description: Split pretrained weights into magnitude and direction and adapt them separately.

lora_init.label: Informed adapter initialisation
lora_init.description: Initialise the low-rank factors from the pretrained weights (SVD) or to absorb quantization error.

parameter_sharing.label: Parameter sharing / structured factors
parameter_sharing.description: Share or factorise adapter parameters across layers (Kronecker, hypercomplex, shared random matrices).

lr_asymmetry.label: Asymmetric learning rates
lr_asymmetry.description: Use different learning rates for the two low-rank factors.

frozen_projection.label: Frozen projection matrix
frozen_projection.description: Freeze one of the low-rank factors to avoid storing activations.

periodic_merge_restart.label: Periodic merge-and-restart
periodic_merge_restart.description: Merge low-rank updates into the weights and restart, accumulating a high-rank change.

quantization.label: Quantization
quantization.description: Represent weights / states in 8-, 4- or fewer bits.

module_composition.label: Module composition / merging
module_composition.description: Combine separately trained adapters, LoRAs or weights (fusion, task arithmetic, averaging).

expert_routing.label: Mixture-of-experts routing
expert_routing.description: Route inputs or training steps across several adaptation modules.

prompt_transfer.label: Prompt transfer
prompt_transfer.description: Initialise a target-task prompt from one learned on source tasks.

low_rank_gradient.label: Low-rank gradient projection
low_rank_gradient.description: Project gradients onto a low-rank subspace to shrink optimizer state while training all weights.

optimizer_state_compression.label: Optimizer-state compression
optimizer_state_compression.description: Shrink or page the optimizer states (8-bit optimizers, paged optimizers, projected states).

activation_recomputation.label: Gradient checkpointing
activation_recomputation.description: Drop activations in the forward pass and recompute them in the backward pass.

mixed_precision.label: Mixed-precision training
mixed_precision.description: Compute in half precision with a full-precision master copy.

sparse_attention.label: Sparse / shifted attention
sparse_attention.description: Approximate full attention with sparse patterns during adaptation to reach long contexts.

serving_system.label: Multi-adapter serving system
serving_system.description: Memory management and batching so thousands of adapters can be served from one base model.

instruction_tuning.label: Instruction tuning
instruction_tuning.description: Fine-tune on tasks phrased as natural-language instructions.

synthetic_instructions.label: Self-generated instruction data
synthetic_instructions.description: Have a model bootstrap its own instruction-tuning data.

curated_data.label: Small curated data
curated_data.description: Replace volume with a few carefully curated examples.

preference_alignment.label: Learning from human feedback
preference_alignment.description: Align outputs to human preferences using human feedback / RL.

weight_regularization.label: Importance-weighted regularisation
weight_regularization.description: Penalise changes to weights that mattered for earlier tasks (EWC).

unified_framework.label: Unified framework / hybrid
unified_framework.description: Casts several PEFT methods in one framework or gates between them.

scale_gap.label: Gap between small and large models

budget_allocation.label: Where to spend the parameter budget (rank selection)

superficial_alignment.label: Knowledge is acquired in pre-training; alignment is superficial

ADDITIVE.description: Inject new trainable parameters; the backbone stays frozen.

SELECTIVE.description: Train only a chosen subset of the existing parameters.

REPARAMETERIZATION.description: Express the weight update in a cheaper form (low-rank, shared, decomposed ...).

COMPRESSION.description: Shrink the numeric representation of the model.

COMPOSITION.description: Combine, route or transfer between separately trained modules.

TRAINING_RECIPE_AND_SYSTEMS.description: Change how training / serving is executed (memory, optimizer, schedule, kernels) rather than what is learned.

SUPERVISION.description: Change the data or objective used to adapt a model.

HYBRID.description: Unify or jointly use several families.
